- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.3) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; increase forecast slightly to avoid missing downward momentum.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overcorrects and forecasts a prolonged decline; reduce forecast slope to reflect mean reversion.
- If model forecast is significantly below true outcome (e.g., >5% gap) and sentiment is rising, model is underreacting; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to capture sentiment-driven rebound.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period price peaks (especially after sentiment spikes); apply a 1–2% upward bias to final 5–7 days of forecast.
- If sentiment history shows rapid reversal (e.g., from 0.8 to 0.1 in 3 days), model often fails to adjust; apply a 2–4% downward correction to forecast 3–5 days ahead.
